name: Barossa

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo and Dolcetto fully without cooking off their freshness.
Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
